q: How do I calculate the emissions of charging electric buses at a depot?
title: Electric bus depot charging emissions
short: Take the depot charger electricity from its meter, multiply by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, and divide by bus kilometres run. The company with operational control of the depot and buses reports it as Scope 2; an authority contracting the service records it in Scope 3.
audience: Bus operators, city transport undertakings and fleet owners

ul: Charger kWh, separate from depot lighting and workshops.
Bus kilometres from the fleet system.
Any opportunity charging away from the depot.

p: Under contracts where an operator runs buses for a transport authority, write down who has operational control of the depot and the buses, and who pays the power bill. Under the operational control approach, that decides whose Scope 2 it is.
Divide by passenger-km as well when ticket data allows, so electric and diesel routes can be compared on the same basis.

example.title: Worked example: one depot, one month (illustrative inputs)
lines: Depot charging electricity: 210,000 kWh x 0.710 = 149,100 kg CO2
example.note: Readings are illustrative; use the depot charger meter and fleet km records.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and fuel card statements (diesel 2.68 and CNG 2.69 kg CO2, IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 record. Hired transport goes to the Scope 3 evidence trail, and distance or tonne-km estimates are labelled as estimates.
